svg.title: BoatAutonomy stern-first slip approach
svg.desc: Diagram in two scenes: numerous environmental factors (left) -- wind, current, and a degraded single-engine boat approaching a two-sided slip -- and automated sensing, guidance, and eventually control (right) -- distance and obstacle sensing, a recommended safe boarding point, and tie-up points, alongside current telemetry, pilot gate, and future gated control requests with no line drawn to the vessel.
svg.text: Stern-first docking target: observe, replay, advise, and gate any future control
What the boater is up against (left); how the system helps reduce that risk (right).

g.text: Dashboard concept - beyond the OEM gauges
current - out from under dock, pushes stern out of slip

svg.text: The cluster sees; the captain authorizes; control remains gated.

g.text: Nature can make docking a risk-filled adventure.
Automated sensing, guidance, and eventually control
BoatAutonomy helps bring order to the chaos.
Position - a track into the dock, not just a dot

svg.text: future control path, not current public claim -- no line drawn to the vessel
Authority grows only after evidence, replay, safety review, and owner approval.
Solid blue/green: current observations. Dashed gray: planned perception classes. Dashed orange: future owner-gated control requests.
